utterances.text: However, you agree, sir, that that document in front of you or that sketch in front of you says that it's a room for meetings. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: That's what's written. But I did not say that that was it and I did not say that Captain Radic drew that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you know that at an observation post meetings can be held. That's a place where a komandir or commander commands. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You know, sir, that at an observation post, a komandir or commander can command from that location and can also hold meetings at that location. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I do not find this question very clear. Could you rephrase it in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A commander or a komandir commands from the observation post. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No. A commander commands. A company commander is in charge from the observation post. That is not a command. I made you go back three times to tell you that this is not a command. As for meetings, meetings, as such, do not exist; it is a giving out of assignments. An assignment can be issued in the street. Are we going to call that a meeting place or a meeting room, then? No, we are not going to call it that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you know that a company commander commands by issuing orders from an observation post. Isn't that correct; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Three times you asked me one single question. A company commander is not a komandant, and he does not issue commands and that is not a command post. And that is what you were asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can a company commander issue commands from an observation post? It's your answer that he cannot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: A company commander cannot command; he can only issue orders for carrying out a task, an assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that he can issue orders from that observation post, and that's where he does it, from his observation post. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Orders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, a company commander commands from his observation post. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: A company commander commands from his observation post? Or rather, commands, what does this word "commands" mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He has the --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: He issues orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He issues orders from his observation post.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he issues orders in relation to battle actions or actions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You can sit down. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: A company commander conveys orders from the superior command, that is to say that he conveys orders from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he also issues tasks from that command post. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No. An observation post is used for coordinating actions, and an observation post can be at a variety of places, depending on the conditions and the situation involved. So he could not command from the observation post because he gets his orders from the superior command on that. He only carries out orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown a Defence exhibit which is 2D02-0050, at page 0098, which is the JNA infantry company rules. The English is DA09-9255 to DA09-9488. It's page 9 in the English, section 214 in both the English and the B/C/S, on page 0098.

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before the witness is given the opportunity to answer this question, before we got the schedule for this witness's testimony, we got a list of documents that would possibly be used by the OTP during his cross-examination; however, this document is not on that list, so I believe that this question cannot be put to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is their document. This is the infantry rules which they supplied to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That doesn't meet the concern of Ms. Tapuskovic, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- in the Chamber's view, Ms. Tapuskovic, the use of this document clearly flows out of the answers that have just been given by your witness to questions. He is appearing to resort to JNA doctrine to answer the questions, so Mr. Weiner is showing him the infantry doctrine of the JNA. We will find out shortly to what point. So, Mr. Weiner, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At page 0098, please. Section 214, it should be a page or two before. 214. Yes. Thank you. Page 97.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Section 214: "The observation post of a company/platoon commander is located in a position providing the most advantageous conditions for commanding the units during the attack." Is that what it says there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could you please show me the beginning of the rules, what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: The first page, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: There's a clearer page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It says: "Rules, Infantry, Mountain Alpine Company-Platoon, 1977."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we go back to page 97 --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you have a chance to read that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 97, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say something to you. It says here "Rule Company." Is that right? I was a company officer, after all, and I know what my duties and responsibilities were specifically in that position. The rules -- sorry, I'm not a lawyer. I did not prepare for this. I know what the duties and tasks of our unit were. As for this, well, yes, I see it's written there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And can we go to the third paragraph in that rule, and it says: "A company commander commands from his observation post from locations or vehicles travelling behind the front lines/axis platoons from which he can best influence the progress of his subordinates' operations." But you see in the beginning it says: "He commands from his observation post." Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I've just told you, these rules, if I can put it specifically -- I'm not really interested in this. I know what my duties were. I was a company officer. Another thing, you're showing me these rules now. I see it says "Rules" and I see some date, but you prove it to me that this is a reliable document, in view of the situation I had in Belgrade vis-a-vis your colleagues. As far as I'm concerned, these rules -- I was not preparing for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: Is that what it says there, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I told you, I'm not interested in the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So, sir, when you said --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I'm not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you said a company commander did not command from his observation post, you were wrong. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No. I was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the rules of the Yugoslav People's Army, which were supplied to us by the Defence counsel for Captain Radic, are incorrect or wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. I said to you specifically: In view of the situation and in view of these tasks that we had, the rules -- I was not preparing for the rules. I'm not familiar with the rules. I'm not a lawyer. So I would kindly ask you, as far as the rules go, not to put questions of that kind to me anymore, but specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, having seen the rules of the army that you belonged to in 1991 that a company commander commands from his observation post, will you now accept that a company commander commands from an observation post? Will you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Receiving orders and carrying out an order is the same as commanding a company. I used the expression of receiving orders and carrying out orders. I have cautioned you already: I was not preparing for the rules. He received orders and carried them out. You can interpret it any way you want. But he would receive an order and carry out an order, carry it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you know who Major Tesic is, who was the battalion commander. You know who that person is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No, no -- oh, Tesic, Major Tesic, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that Major Tesic testified in Belgrade that Captain Radic had a command post? Would that surprise you, sir? And that was on 15 December 2004.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: The company commander had an observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The question is, sir: Would it surprise you that Major Tesic has testified in a court in Belgrade that Captain Radic had a command post? Would that surprise you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Captain Radic had an observation post. The comments of Major Tesic in this particular case -- well, I know that this was an observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know who Sasa Bojkovski is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: A company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that he testified also in Belgrade that Captain Radic had his command on Nova Street? Would that surprise you, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Captain Radic had an observation post, and you ask Major Tesic and this Captain Bojkovski why they did not read what you are putting to me now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that it was Captain Bojkovski who recommended to Captain Radic that he should use that particular house, and that's what he stated? And after stating that, he stated that was where his command was. Does that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to repeat this question once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that Captain Bojkovski, who, according to his statement, was the person who recommended to Captain Radic that he use that house as his observation post, stated that that was his command? Does that surprise you, too, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: As for this last matter, I'm telling you, yet again, it was an observation post. Now, who was it was who proposed this, I would not like to discuss that, as far as these statements of yours are concerned. It is the company commander who decides where the company station will be, where the observation post will be, where one observation post will be, where another observation post will be, depending on the needs involved. So Company Commander Bojkovski, as you had put it, I don't know what he was doing in our sector, or rather, on our axis. It would be the same as if I were to sit there with you and if I were to teach you your job. Captain Bojkovski had his job -- his company and Captain Radic had his own company, and one should not interfere with the other's work. One knows exactly when one should do what and where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, would it surprise you that a person has testified in this court, at page 10.377, that frequent meetings were held there on the eve of combat actions? Are you denying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Please, could you reformulate this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we've had testimony before this Court that frequent meetings were held at that observation post prior to combat actions. Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I understood the first part about the witness, let's say, but this second part I would like to ask you to specify more concretely which assignment when. That part is not clear to me. The first part is clear to me; the second part is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, there has been testimony in this court that frequent meetings were held at that observation post prior to - whether you want to call it combat operations - military actions. Do you deny that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: That is not correct. There were no meetings at the observation post. I note I'm telling the truth and only the truth, what was. I'm not interested in other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not even in the meeting room, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: What do you mean, in the meeting room?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In the room on the sketch which Captain Radic drew and designated "in the room where meetings were held"? So no meetings were held in that room, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Meetings in the sense of meetings, no. I mentioned this before. This was a company station. If Captain Radic called me, or Lieutenant Hadzic, and asked us to sit and to look at the decision, then you can understand that as a meeting, but as a meeting with his subordinates. But actually meetings were held at another place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, there's also been testimony that that observation post was a headquarters, an operations headquarters, for the military actions occurring in the area. Do you deny that, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: You mean our observation post? It was an observation post, not a command post, and there were no meetings held there and nobody came to the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A person who stayed there and was a member of that company has testified that daily meetings were held at that observation post. Do you deny that, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: That it was an observation post, yes; as for meetings being held there an a daily basis, no. Specifically, meetings of the company commander were held at the battalion command located in the Svetozara Markovica Street. Perhaps you didn't know that, but let me tell you. That's where the meetings were held and that's where --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question was -- sir, the question was: Do you deny it; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I deny that there were meetings. There were no meetings at our observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That same person who lived there and was a member of your company has testified that plans for the following day's combat actions were decided at these meetings. Are you denying that testimony, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That same person who lived there and was a member of your company had testified that plans for the following day's combat actions were decided at these meetings. Are you denying that testimony, too, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I don't know what to say about that testimony. On his return from the battalion command, Captain Radic, in that meeting, would decide, on the basis of the working map, and plan the activities for the following day. Earlier, you say the person living there, that he was a member, or rather, a member of our unit. No. Captain Radic, when he received an assignment, would there use a lamp and plan and organise actions for the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Another member of your company has testified that daily meetings were held at that observation post and that Captain Radic had the final say on those combat matters. Are you denying that testimony, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to explain to me who were the persons he had the meetings with so that I would be able to give you a specific answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: First my question and then we can go into private session. But first my question: Another member of that company has testified that meetings were held there on a daily basis and that Captain Radic had the final say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: First, meetings were not held there. Captain Radic could not have had the final say. In relation to whom, I don't know. But I know that Captain Radic would study the assignment he received from the battalion command on his return from meetings that were held regularly in the evening. So he would go over the assignments himself for purposes of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One more witness, and then we'll go into private session and ask you the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One more witness and we must have the break, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you like to have the break now before I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. I apologise. I wasn't watching the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We must now adjourn because the tapes are running out. We'll resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, a Defence witness for Mr. Mrksic, who's not associated with those three other witnesses that we mentioned, has testified that meetings were held at that house and he even attended one. First question: Do you know who Dusan Jaskic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you recall a Mr. Dusan Jaskic, who was from Vukovar, the Petrova Gora area, who was tied to the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No, I don't know the name. The first and the last name are not familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you were never present in the house when Mr. Jaskic visited and attended a meeting there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: The observation post is a place where the commander of the company is. So how can I explain it to you? It's not a railway station. It's not a room where anybody can pass through. It's an observation post. It's not possible for anybody to enter whenever they want. So those who were not part of our group, who were not our JNA soldiers or had no contacts with Captain Radic, wouldn't be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Jaskic also testified that Captain Radic would discuss plans with soldiers there. Do you deny that, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Captain Radic, from what I recall, did not have contact with people at the observation post who were not part of our group, especially not with the gentleman whom you just named. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just said, from what you recall. You were not always at that location. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: During those five, 10 minutes, 15 minutes, 20 minutes, when I went to the other company station, I don't believe that anybody could come and have meetings or make plans. The time would be too short for an assertion that you are making. Well, I was away from the observation post for five or 15 minutes at the most, from the observation post, because that's where the materiel was, there, that could possibly be subject to theft; weapons, ammunition. I had to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, so on a daily basis, seven days a week, you were away from the observation post ten -- between five and 15 minutes a day? So you were at the observation post 23 hours and 45 minutes every day? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: As you said, 23 hours is a lot at a stretch, but I was never away at any point for longer than that. Perhaps at some point I could go to the toilet or something, I don't know. But I was never absent for 23 hours, as you said, from the observation post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, sir. I'm saying it's your testimony that you were at the observation post for 23 hours and 45 minutes per day, apparently seven days a week.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to be more specific with this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm being very specific, sir. You said you were at the observation -- you were away from the observation post between five and 15 minutes a day. So I just want to get your testimony down. Are you claiming you were at that observation post 23 hours and 45 minutes per day, every day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: This, again, is not clear to me. But I was carrying out assignments. In the course of the day, Captain Radic would go out for combat, and perhaps at the time he was at the other observation post. But this was still a company station. But he might go still to another place during the day. Wherever the commander of the company was, that's where the observation post was. But this observation post would then switch locations depending on the combat actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we're speaking not about multiple observation posts; we're speaking about one particular post, the post of Stanko's father or Stanko Vujanovic's family, the family compound. That's the only one, not the others. And you know you were away from there at various times during the day. You were supplying -- you were going to Negoslavci for supplies; you were going to the other observation post; you were meeting with other soldiers. You were away from there during the day and, on occasion, in evenings, too. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: 23 hours and 45 minutes I was at the observation post, as you said, or I was away for that amount of time during the day. I didn't understand that part before. That's what's the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. The last time I'll ask it: You said you were only away from the observation post between five and 15 minutes a day. So are you saying you were there for 23 hours and 45 minutes a day, every day? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honours, before the witness responds to the answer, we have been talking about 23 hours and 45 minutes. On page 59, line 22, the witness said that perhaps he was away for five, ten, 15, or 20 minutes. So perhaps, then, we could keep in mind the answer of the witness and then make the time delineation and then see, on the basis of that, how we could determine the actual amount of time, and not just stick to 23 hours and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: At the suggestion of Defence counsel, I'll switch to 23 hours and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is that what you're saying, that you were at that house 23 hours and 40 minutes a day, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time. I mean, I had assignments; I've already said that. So I wasn't really counting. But what you're asking me, this time-period, 23 hours and 45 minutes, Captain Radic was not at that place, he was not at that observation post. What I said was that nobody, especially not the gentleman whom you named, came there. So it's impossible for me to be at the company station and Captain Radic to be in action and then, as you say, to have meetings organised. Who could these meetings have been organised with when Captain Radic was on combat actions? That's why I don't see there how much time I spent there in the course of the day, because everybody had assignments, activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you weren't there 24 hours a day, you can't state what happened while you were away, can you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I can say something about the time that I did spend there at the observation post, so I'm talking about that time. And the gentleman whom you mentioned did not come to these, as you say, meetings. I do not know the gentleman, and no one actually came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But, sir, as you said, since you weren't there, you can't state what happened while you were away from that observation post.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I was away from the observation post during the morning, mostly, for two to three hours at the most. That's when combat actions were being conducted, and Captain Radic was not at the observation post then. It's not possible for him to be in two places at the same time, in combat and at the observation post to hold meetings. So during the time that I spent there, I did not see them there. And I'm also asserting that nobody came there. It was a unit, after all, and not everyone could just come and enter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So, sir, if we'd summarise this, it's your testimony that all these other people, including those who were not even related to each other, who testified about the meetings being held there, are all wrong; that's your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I'm speaking for myself and what I saw. I cannot say anything about others. Anyone is free to say whatever they want. I'm telling you what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, you've been telling us what you saw and what you've recalled. You were in Vukovar for almost two months. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that. A little bit less than two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I think it's fair to say that it was a stressful time for you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Yes, it was -- combat actions were going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you were quite young at the time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I think you can agree that it wasn't a happy occasion for you, to be there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I was there under orders. As to whether it was a happy occasion or not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, people were being killed; people were being injured; there was firing or shooting. That's not a happy occasion, is it, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I would just like to say -- to go back to that part that was in private session. I told you what my qualifications were, what school I completed. It was a school with a name and it had something to teach us; amongst other things, precisely what you said, how to overcome stressful situations, how to deal with that, and so on and so forth. I'm a professional in my work. I was a professional then and I'm more of a professional now, with more experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And would you agree, sir, that it was a stressful situation and it's not something that you want to think about regularly, that time back in Vukovar. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: That event in itself is not a pleasant one, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you don't think or talk about that on a regular basis. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Since that year, this is now the first time that I'm talking about it. I thought -- when you sent me the questions, the question that referred to the waiver on keeping military secrets, so it started from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This is the second or third time today you said, "When you sent me the questions." Are you referring to me in particular? Are you saying that I sent you something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstood. What I meant was the Prosecutor's office. Not you personally, but the Prosecutor's office. I'm seeing you for the first time yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you said, "Since that year, this is now the first time that I'm talking about." So after Vukovar, you didn't speak to your fellow soldiers about that; isn't that correct? Meaning your experiences in Vukovar, you weren't talking about it regularly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No. It was an event. The combat actions finished. Things went on as they did. I continued with my military career until this point, until two days ago when I received the questions, and this is when this was re-activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were very young and I would assume that you didn't maintain a diary while you were in Vukovar as to what occurred each day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I did not keep a diary before, as a child; I don't keep a diary now. I'm talking about myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Nor, I assume, have you kept a calendar or any sort of records of what occurred each day, whether it's writing notes in a calendar or writing notes of any kind. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No, I didn't have a calendar. I don't know what dates on a calendar would mean to you. That doesn't mean anything to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And having not kept any sort of calendar or diary and having not discussed this matter in almost 15 years, would it be fair to say that you're relying strictly on your memory as to times, dates, places, happenings? Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I'm happy that that's the way it is and that I still rely on my memory and on my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, I have one final question. I wrote a note to myself while you were testifying about the observation post. You said that you kept the ammunition there; that's why -- it was another reason you had to be there. Is that your testimony, you kept it at the observation post?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it was the other observation post, Mr. Weiner, two of them, two different streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Maybe that needs to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can I ask -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us: Where did you keep the ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as for what the witness's task was exactly is something that we discussed in private session, so I would like to ask my colleague that, if he wants to deal with that, if he wants to follow that line of questioning, that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in public session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that you went to the hospital on November 19th, 1991. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you went there with Captain Radic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Captain Radic and the rest of the troops and Lieutenant Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you claim to have gone there on orders from Major Tesic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you testified that you were in Captain Radic's presence when he received a notice to go there from Captain Tesic. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: He did not receive notice; he received an order. I think that these two concepts are very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the Defence is required to file summaries of your anticipated testimony. In the first summary, there is no indication that you were present when Captain Radic allegedly received that order. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I haven't read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you tell the Defence that --

utterances.speaker: MS. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. I'm sorry, Your Honours. Just a moment. Before me now I have the first summary of the Defence that was submitted to the Court on the 11th of July, if I remember correctly. Item 4 says: "The witness, after the fall of Vukovar, together with the accused Miroslav Radic and some members of their company, went to the Vukovar hospital." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm asking him specifically about alleged orders by Captain Radic -- I'm sorry, Major Tesic which he claims he was present for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Present when a radio message was received on a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you previously provide that information to the Defence, that you were present when Captain Radic received an order from Major Tesic to secure the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: That evening, I do not remember. I was tired when we first met here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, prior to that, if we go to the second statement on July 31st, 2006, again, there is no indication that you ever told -- I'm sorry, you were ever present with Captain Radic when he allegedly received an order from Major Tesic to secure the hospital. Are you certain that you told -- or do you know whether you told the Defence at some later time about that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Could I ask you to repeat the date for me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure, sir. That's July 31st, 2006.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: May I just take a piece of paper from here?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: As for all events in Vukovar, from the 13th of September, the lawyer, Mr. Borovic, and the Defence could talk about all of that to me and you could talk from the 28th onwards, from the moment when I was granted the waiver. As for this date that you gave in July, I don't know who it was that I talked to, because after the 13th of September I could make a statement and communicate with someone. In July, I did not have the paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you know -- you have no idea who provided any of the information in your anticipated testimony sheets or basically with regard to the summaries of your anticipated summary? You have no idea who provided this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Let us say that the first meeting with the people from the Defence was when I arrived, only in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, in the most recent proofing notes dated 12 October 2006, the only mention of Major Tesic is, I quote, "that he saw Major Tesic in front of the hospital." Again, my question is: Did you ever say to anyone that you were present when Major Tesic contacted Radic and ordered him to go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: If you mean the date that you mentioned to me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, is it possible that you went to the hospital on November 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I am sorry, but what hospital? Who are you talking about? Are you talking about me or somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Is it possible you went to the Vukovar Hospital on November 18th, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: No, the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, since you were in Negoslavci on the 18th, you don't know whether or not Captain Radic also went there on the 18th. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: The first units that crossed the Vuka was that group headed by Captain Radic, Lieutenant Hadzic, I, and the soldiers, on the 19th of November. So that was the first crossing, across the Vuka in the direction of the hospital, and in terms of arriving at the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, Captain Sasa Bojkovski, who is another company commander, has given a statement indicating that he went to the hospital and saw Captain Radic and it was either November 17th or 18th. Does that refresh your recollection that Captain Radic was there on the 18th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: Well, if you're trying to impose something, you cannot. On the 19th, we entered the area of the hospital, on the 19th in the morning hours. What Bojkovski did and what you are saying, I don't know about that. I know that our unit was given the task on the 19th, and on the 19th the hospital was secured.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, Major Tesic has given a statement at the court in Belgrade that Radic was not at that hospital pursuant to his orders but, rather, Radic was at that hospital in violation of his orders. Does that surprise you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I would not like to use any other kind of vocabulary now, but I know that Captain Radic received orders from Major Tesic. I would not like to comment upon anyone's statements. I know what it was that I heard and what it was that was ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that Captain Tesic was in a much better position than you to know what his orders were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 2D4
utterances.text: I know what it was that I heard and what it was that was ordered. Also, Captain Radic knows what he heard and what order he received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was going to go into another area in relation to the hospital. Would it be best to break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it becomes necessary because of the hour. The evidence will have to continue on Monday, at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of October, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
